description: We are a team of passionate and creative individuals who are excited about technology, innovation, and exploring new possibilities. Our main interests are web development and game development, and we are eager to use our creativity and technical skills to build something meaningful and innovative
summary:
We developed Astro Rangers: Outpost Survival, an interactive browser-based Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that transforms space education into a hands-on mission experience. Instead of only learning about astronauts through textbooks, videos, or lectures, players become junior astronauts and make decisions while completing a simulated space mission.

The experience takes players through astronaut training, lunar survival, base-building challenges, emergency situations, and a return mission to Earth. Their choices and performance affect the mission, helping them understand that space exploration requires problem-solving, preparation, and responsible decision-making.

Our project addresses the challenge by making astronaut training more interactive, engaging, and accessible. It is important because it encourages young people to explore STEM, think critically under pressure, and understand that astronauts must apply scientific knowledge to real situations—not simply memorize facts.
details:
Astro Rangers: Outpost Survival is a browser-based interactive learning experience designed as a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. The player begins by creating a junior astronaut, choosing a space companion, and selecting a mission mode. The training then progresses through a structured journey: preparation on Earth, survival and decision-making on the Moon, completing mission challenges, responding to emergencies, and successfully returning to Earth.

Rather than presenting information only through passive lessons, our project uses gameplay to simulate the responsibilities and challenges astronauts face. Players must complete tasks, manage mission conditions, and make decisions that can affect their progress. This creates a stronger connection between scientific knowledge and practical problem-solving.

The main benefit of the project is experiential learning. Young people can explore space science while actively participating in a mission, which can make complex STEM topics more engaging and memorable. Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space exploration and encourage the next generation to develop critical thinking, resilience, technical awareness, and decision-making skills.

We developed the project as a web application using REACT, VIEW JS. SI helped us to develop a prototype, 3d design and functions, making it accessible directly through a browser without requiring specialized hardware or software. We focused on creating an intuitive interface, clear mission progression, interactive challenges, and game mechanics that provide immediate feedback to the player. We used NASA recourses such as DONKI, OSDR and RadLab

Our project is creative because it combines education, storytelling, simulation, and game design into one continuous astronaut experience. We considered accessibility, ease of use, engagement, age-appropriate learning, mission realism, and the importance of showing that astronauts must make thoughtful decisions when facing unexpected challenges. The result is not simply a space quiz, but an interactive environment where young people can learn by experiencing the mission themselves.
